### Shape

#### Description

A GitHub Actions workflow in this application's own repository, `.github/workflows/edge.yml`, builds and publishes an edge release for each push to its `main` branch, and for nothing else: not pull requests, not other branches, and not tags. It runs once per push, for the commit at its head. Edge releases are nightly-like builds of whatever main holds, not stable releases, and are marked as such.

#### Version

An edge release's version is `0.1.N`, where N is the commit's sequence number on main: how many commits its history holds, counted by `git rev-list --count` on that commit, so each commit on main has its own number, one more than its parent's, and the same commit always gets the same version. The workflow checks out the whole history to count it, never a shallow clone.
The version is baked into the binary when it is built, so the application knows its own version. A build made anywhere else, as on a developer's machine, has the version Cargo.toml gives it.

#### Builds

The application is built in release mode, one job per platform, run side by side, each on a GitHub-hosted runner of that platform:

- Linux, x86_64, on Ubuntu
- Windows, x86_64
- macOS, Apple silicon, aarch64

Each job runs the project's tests before building, and installs whatever the platform needs to build the application's GUI, as Linux's windowing and font libraries. Each builds from the repository as it is at that commit, the default prompts in `.suspense/system-prompts` included, as the application's build needs them. The Windows binary is a GUI application, opening no console of its own, as the [ApplicationScope](../application/index.md#application-scope) says.

#### Publishing

Once every platform's job has succeeded, one GitHub release is published for the commit, tagged `v0.1.N` on that commit, titled "Suspense 0.1.N (edge)", and marked as a pre-release, never as the latest stable release. Its notes give the commit's short hash, linked to the commit, and its message's first line.
Its assets are one archive per platform, each holding the binary alone, named for the version and the platform:

- `suspense-0.1.N-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`
- `suspense-0.1.N-windows-x86_64.zip`
- `suspense-0.1.N-macos-aarch64.tar.gz`

The binaries are not signed or notarized.
If any platform's job fails, nothing is published for that commit, so no edge release ever lacks a platform; the workflow run shows which job failed. A release already published for a version, as when a run is re-run, is never published twice: the run publishes nothing more for it and succeeds.
Pushes are handled in the order they came: a run waits for the one before it to finish rather than cancelling it, so every commit on main gets its edge release. The workflow is given only the permission it needs to publish, writing the repository's contents, and uses the token GitHub gives each run, needing no secrets of its own.

# Builds Suspense for Linux, macOS, and Windows whenever something is merged
# into the release branch, and publishes a zip for each as a GitHub release
# named for the version and the build of the day: Suspense 0.1.0 (2026-09-17.2).
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [release]
  workflow_dispatch:

# One release at a time, so two on the same day can't take the same number.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  # Names the build once, so every platform's zip carries the same name.
  name:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.name.outputs.version }}
      build: ${{ steps.name.outputs.build }}
      bundle_version: ${{ steps.name.outputs.bundle_version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.name.outputs.tag }}
      title: ${{ steps.name.outputs.title }}
      file: ${{ steps.name.outputs.file }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: name
        run: |
          .github/scripts/build-name.sh | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build:
    needs: name
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: linux-x86_64
            os: ubuntu-22.04
          - platform: macos-universal
            os: macos-14
          - platform: windows-x86_64
            os: windows-latest
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    env:
      # What the zip, and the folder inside it, are called.
      PACKAGE: ${{ needs.name.outputs.file }}-${{ matrix.platform }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install system libraries
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            pkg-config libxkbcommon-dev libxkbcommon-x11-dev libwayland-dev \
            libx11-xcb-dev libxcb1-dev libfontconfig-dev libfreetype-dev \
            libvulkan-dev

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          # Both Mac architectures, for one universal app.
          targets: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && 'aarch64-apple-darwin,x86_64-apple-darwin' || '' }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: ${{ matrix.platform }}

      - name: Build (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked
          mkdir -p "dist/$PACKAGE"
          cp target/release/suspense LICENSE.md "dist/$PACKAGE/"
          cd dist && zip -r "../$PACKAGE.zip" "$PACKAGE"

      - name: Build (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin
          cargo build --release --locked --target x86_64-apple-darwin
          app="dist/$PACKAGE/Suspense.app"
          mkdir -p "$app/Contents/MacOS"
          lipo -create -output "$app/Contents/MacOS/suspense" \
            target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/suspense \
            target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/suspense
          sed -e "s/@VERSION@/${{ needs.name.outputs.version }}/g" \
            -e "s/@BUNDLE_VERSION@/${{ needs.name.outputs.bundle_version }}/g" \
            packaging/macos/Info.plist > "$app/Contents/Info.plist"
          mkdir -p "$app/Contents/Resources"
          cp packaging/icons/suspense.icns "$app/Contents/Resources/Suspense.icns"
          cp LICENSE.md "dist/$PACKAGE/"
          # ditto keeps the bundle's permissions and structure intact.
          cd dist && ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent "$PACKAGE" "../$PACKAGE.zip"

      - name: Build (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "dist/$env:PACKAGE" | Out-Null
          Copy-Item target/release/suspense.exe, LICENSE.md "dist/$env:PACKAGE/"
          Compress-Archive -Path "dist/$env:PACKAGE" -DestinationPath "$env:PACKAGE.zip"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ env.PACKAGE }}
          path: ${{ env.PACKAGE }}.zip
          if-no-files-found: error

  # Once all three have built, they're published together as one release.
  publish:
    needs: [name, build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Publish the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.name.outputs.tag }}
          TITLE: ${{ needs.name.outputs.title }}
        run: |
          gh release create "$TAG" dist/*.zip \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --target "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --title "$TITLE" \
            --notes "Built from ${{ github.sha }} on the release branch."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Names a release build: the version from Cargo.toml, today's date (UTC), and
# which build of the day this is, counting the releases already tagged today.
#
#   Suspense 0.1.0 (2026-09-17.2)
#
# Prints, one per line, for $GITHUB_OUTPUT:
#   version=0.1.0
#   build=2026-09-17.2                         shown in the name
#   bundle_version=20260917.2                  macOS's CFBundleVersion: numbers and dots
#   tag=v0.1.0-2026-09-17.2
#   title=Suspense 0.1.0 (2026-09-17.2)
#   file=Suspense-0.1.0-2026-09-17.2           the start of each zip's name
#
# Tags are read with `git ls-remote --tags`, from $TAGS_FROM (default origin).
# $TODAY overrides the date, for testing.
set -euo pipefail

version=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml | head -1)
today=${TODAY:-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)}

# The highest sequence already tagged for this version today.
last=$(git ls-remote --tags "${TAGS_FROM:-origin}" "v${version}-${today}.*" \
  | sed -n "s|.*refs/tags/v${version}-${today}\.\([0-9][0-9]*\)$|\1|p" \
  | sort -n | tail -1)
sequence=$(( ${last:-0} + 1 ))

build="${today}.${sequence}"
echo "version=${version}"
echo "build=${build}"
echo "bundle_version=${today//-/}.${sequence}"
echo "tag=v${version}-${build}"
echo "title=Suspense ${version} (${build})"
echo "file=Suspense-${version}-${build}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Names a release build: the version from Cargo.toml, today's date (UTC), and
# which build of the day this is, counting the releases already tagged today.
#
#   Suspense 0.1.0 (2026-09-17.2)

I've added the edge release workflow, but it hasn't run yet: it only starts on a push to GitHub. All 481 tests pass on Linux, and the YAML parses. Your next push to `main` would publish about `v0.1.67`.

**The workflow (`.github/workflows/edge.yml`)**
- **Trigger:** every push to `main`, and nothing else.
- **Version:** worked out once from the full history as `0.1.$(git rev-list --count HEAD)`, so all three platforms use the same number.
- **Builds:** three jobs side by side — Linux x86_64 on `ubuntu-24.04`, Windows x86_64 on `windows-latest`, macOS Apple silicon on `macos-14`. Each runs `cargo test --locked`, then `cargo build --release --locked`, with the version passed in. Linux installs the GUI libraries your CI workflow already uses. The Windows release build already has no console.
- **Archives:** `suspense-0.1.N-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, `suspense-0.1.N-windows-x86_64.zip` and `suspense-0.1.N-macos-aarch64.tar.gz`, each holding only the binary.
- **Publishing:** once all three succeed, one release is created, tagged `v0.1.N` on that commit and titled "Suspense 0.1.N (edge)". It's marked as a pre-release and never as "latest". Its notes are the short hash, linked to the commit, plus the first line of the commit message.
- **Safety:** if any platform fails, nothing is published. A re-run of an already-released commit succeeds without publishing anything more. Runs queue in push order and never cancel each other. The workflow only has `contents: write` and uses the run's own token.

**In the app:** the new `src/version.rs` holds the version: `SUSPENSE_VERSION` when the workflow sets it, otherwise `Cargo.toml`'s `0.1.0`. A version nothing reads is dropped from the binary, so I added `suspense --version` to print it, which the spec doesn't mention. I checked it prints `0.1.999` when built with that value and `0.1.0` normally.

**Things to know**
- **Tests on Windows and macOS have never run.** Your existing CI only tests on Linux, so some tests may fail there the first time. If one does, nothing is published until it's fixed.
- **Existing workflows unchanged:** the CI workflow and the date-named `release.yml` for the `release` branch stay as they were. You may want to remove `release.yml` if edge builds replace it.
- **Unsigned binaries:** they aren't signed or notarized, so macOS and Windows will warn the first time they're opened.

**Spec build:** the host `piton build` failed at first on an unowned reference file, `edge-releases/index.md`. That's the case last turn's retry handles, but the app that ran the spec step was built before that change. I deleted that one file and the build then wrote 77 files.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791091004-CrossPlatformReleaseCIPipeline2.understanding.md`.
